# A loop over one slice that writes another is limited by the slice it ranges over.
# With a destination longer than the source the vector loop used to run forever: it
# was bounded by len(dst), and loading from the exhausted source returns no
# elements. A destination shorter than the source panics, as the scalar loop does.

exec go run ./testmain
cmp stdout testmain/output

cp ops.go ops.go.orig
loopvec -split .
! stdout .
cmpenv stderr stderr.want
cmp ops_simd.go ops_simd.go.want

env GOEXPERIMENT=simd
exec go run ./testmain
cmp stdout testmain/output

-- go.mod --
module example.com/test

go 1.27.1
-- ops.go --
package test

func Scale(dst, src []float32, f float32) {
	for i, v := range src {
		dst[i] = v * f
	}
}
-- ops_simd.go.want --
//go:build goexperiment.simd

package test

import (
	"simd"
	"unsafe"
)

func Scale(dst, src []float32, f float32) {
	_vcFloat32s0 := simd.BroadcastFloat32s(f)
	if _loopvecOverlap(dst, src, 0, len(src), 0, len(src)) {
		for i, v := range src {
			dst[i] = v * f
		}
	} else {
		if len(src) > 0 {
			_ = dst[len(src)-1]
			_ = src[len(src)-1]
			{
				_w1 := dst[:len(src):len(src)]
				_count := len(_w1)
				_w2 := src[:_count:_count]
				_i, _lanes := 0, simd.BroadcastFloat32s(0).Len()
				for ; _i <= _count-4*_lanes; _i += 4 * _lanes {
					_c1, _c2 := _w1[_i:][:4*_lanes], _w2[_i:][:4*_lanes]
					_v1 := simd.LoadFloat32s(_c2)
					_v1.Mul(_vcFloat32s0).Store(_c1)
					_v2 := simd.LoadFloat32s(_c2[_lanes:])
					_v2.Mul(_vcFloat32s0).Store(_c1[_lanes:])
					_v3 := simd.LoadFloat32s(_c2[2*_lanes:])
					_v3.Mul(_vcFloat32s0).Store(_c1[2*_lanes:])
					_v4 := simd.LoadFloat32s(_c2[3*_lanes:])
					_v4.Mul(_vcFloat32s0).Store(_c1[3*_lanes:])
				}
				for ; _i <= _count-_lanes; _i += _lanes {
					_v5 := simd.LoadFloat32s(_w2[_i:])
					_v5.Mul(_vcFloat32s0).Store(_w1[_i:])
				}
				for _i < _count {
					_v6, _n := simd.LoadFloat32sPart(_w2[_i:])
					_v6.Mul(_vcFloat32s0).StorePart(_w1[_i:])
					_i += _n
				}
			}
		}
	}
}

func _loopvecOverlap[T any](a, b []T, window ...int) bool {
	aLo, aHi, bLo, bHi := 0, len(a), 0, len(b)
	if len(window) == 4 {
		aLo, aHi, bLo, bHi = window[0], window[1], window[2], window[3]
	}
	if aLo >= aHi || bLo >= bHi {
		return false
	}
	size := unsafe.Sizeof(a[0])
	aBase := uintptr(unsafe.Pointer(unsafe.SliceData(a)))
	bBase := uintptr(unsafe.Pointer(unsafe.SliceData(b)))
	aStart, aEnd := aBase+uintptr(aLo)*size, aBase+uintptr(aHi)*size
	bStart, bEnd := bBase+uintptr(bLo)*size, bBase+uintptr(bHi)*size
	return aStart < bEnd && bStart < aEnd
}
-- stderr.want --
loopvec: rewrote 1 loop(s) in $WORK/ops.go
-- testmain/main.go --
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"example.com/test"
)

func try(f func()) (panicked bool) {
	defer func() { panicked = recover() != nil }()
	f()
	return
}

func main() {
	dst := make([]float32, 8)
	test.Scale(dst, []float32{1, 2, 3}, 2)
	fmt.Println(dst)
	dst = make([]float32, 3)
	test.Scale(dst, []float32{1, 2, 3}, 2)
	fmt.Println(dst)
	short := make([]float32, 3)
	fmt.Println(try(func() { test.Scale(short, []float32{1, 2, 3, 4, 5}, 2) }))
	untouched := []float32{7, 7, 7, 7}
	test.Scale(untouched, nil, 2)
	fmt.Println(untouched)
}
-- testmain/output --
[2 4 6 0 0 0 0 0]
[2 4 6]
true
[7 7 7 7]
